THROUGH THE WINDOW

Finding it from the window

Watch the north side around Himeji Station: the right-hand windows heading west, the left-hand windows heading east. Look for a white silhouette with several overlapping roofs above the city.

About 1.5 km of city lies between the track and the keep. Buildings interrupt the view, and the close-up photograph makes the castle look much larger than it does to the eye. Use the wider view to find its place among the rooftops, and start watching before the station.

THE CASTLE

The keep behind the view

Himeji keeps the tower Ikeda Terumasa completed in 1609, never lost to fire or war. Its white plaster walls earned it the name White Heron Castle; it became a National Treasure in 1951 and one of Japan's first World Heritage sites in 1993. The main keep is linked to three smaller keeps by covered bridges, which is why it reads as layers rather than a single tower.
